title: Deep-Learning-Based ADHD Classification Using Children's Skeleton Data Acquired through the ADHD Screening Game
summary: A bidirectional LSTM with weighted loss classified clinician-labeled ADHD, ADHD-risk and normal groups from game-acquired skeleton sequences in 596 children; best reported accuracy was 97.82% under leave-one-person-out validation. The source records ADHD-risk cases classified as normal and frames the system as screening support, not diagnosis. Methods §3.4: leave-one-person-out; labels incorporate clinician review and CBCL/K-ARS, but are not independent diagnoses; limitations in §5.
ai_technology: Methods §3.4: GRU/RNN/LSTM sequence classifier, bidirectional layer and weighted cross-entropy on 18-joint skeleton sequences.
organization: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Methods §3.3, Results §4: 596 children and three clinician-labeled groups; 97.82% LSTM and ADHD-risk false-normal errors.
evidence.unknown: Methods §3.4: leave-one-person-out; labels incorporate clinician review and CBCL/K-ARS, but are not independent diagnoses; limitations in §5. The source does not establish benefits beyond the reported evaluation.
